newsitem.title: UK: UK commercial radio market seen growing further.
newsitem.headline: UK commercial radio market seen growing further.

text.p: The UK commercial radio market, which has more than doubled its market share over the last 10 years, is expected to continue to grow, with the advent of digital broadcasting increasing station choices, according to a report released on Tuesday.

"Radio is a resilient medium, as its survival over the second half of the 20th century has shown, and there are strong arguments that radio's strengths will ensure that it survives the advent of the digital age as the most effective communications medium," the Radio Advertising Bureau (RAB) said in its report, "The Future of Commercial Radio".

"While the rate of growth in commercial radio audiences will slow, it's anticipated that the continued growth in choice being made available to listeners will mean future growth for commercial radio audiences," RAB said.

Digital Audio Broadcasting, which is being introduced in Britain under the Broadcasting Act of 1996, will result in greater choice for listeners. The allocation of the new frequencies means that listeners in an average area will have access to eight national BBC stations, eight national commercial stations and 16 local stations.

Although the role of radio has changed greatly since the days when it was a focal point of family evening entertainment, the report noted that 86 percent of UK adults listen to the radio each week. The average adult listens to the radio for just under three hours a day, and the average British household has four radio sets, the RAB said.

Commercial radio was introduced in Britain in 1973, and in 1986 the UK's two commercial radio stations accounted for 27 percent of all radio listening. The share of commercial radio has more than doubled over the last 10 years, with more than 60 percent of listening now accounted for by commercial stations, the report found.

As the commercial listening audience has increased, the attitude of advertisers toward radio has also changed. The amount of money spent on radio advertising almost doubled from 1992 to 1996, with most of the growth coming from national advertisers, the report said.

The rapid growth of commercial radio is similar to the growth patterns in emerging economies. "While it is anticipated that annual growth rates will slow down, industry forecasts predict that commercial radio revenue will continue to grow more quickly than the advertising marketplace as a whole for several years to come," RAB said.

Commercial radio has been forecast to growth at 16 percent in 1996 in an overall advertising market that is growing only six percent. Commercial radio has already posted 18 percent growth in the first half of 1996.

Commercial radio revenues rose 22.9 percent in 1995 to 270.6 million stg ($423 million), accounting for 4.3 percent of display advertising in Britain. The revenues are forecast to reach 487.0 million pounds by 2000 and to account for 5.1 percent of display advertising, RAB reported.
